text.p: Clyde Drexler scored a season-high 36 points, including a driving layup with 1.5 seconds left that gave the red-hot Houston Rockets their 12th win in 13 games, 96-94 over the Minnesota Timberwolves on Tuesday.
The Timberwolves had a chance to tie when Chris Carr took a lob pass and was fouled by Mario Elie with 0.2 seconds left.

But after a Houston timeout, Rockets forward Charles Barkley said something to rattle Carr, who was 7-of-11 from the line this season. Carr missed the first shot and intentionally missed the second, but Minnesota could not tip in the miss and suffered its season-high fifth straight loss.

"Taunting at the free-throw line was an everyday thing in practice last year," said Carr, who was a teammate of Barkley's on the Phoenix Suns last season. "He knows as well as I do that I can't miss those. He said, 'Don't choke.'"
In Atlanta, Steve Smith's 15-foot jumper with 3.9 seconds remaining lifted the Atlanta Hawks to their seventh straight home win, an 89-88 decision over the reeling Denver Nuggets.
Atlanta scored the first two points of the fourth quarter to extend its lead to 70-56 before the Nuggets went on a 16-6 run to cut the gap to 76-72 with 5:37 left.
Denver assumed its first lead since 16-15 when LaPhonso Ellis' jumper made it 88-87 with 42 seconds to play.
Laettner had 22 points and Mookie Blaylock 21 for Atlanta.
In Cleveland, Voshon Lenard's off-balance 15-foot banker as time expired gave the Miami Heat their ninth straight road victory, 76-74 over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Tim Hardaway scored 25 points and Alonzo Mourning added 14 for the Heat.
Chris Mills scored 17 points and Tyrone Hill added 15 points and 13 rebounds for Cleveland.
In Los Angeles, Chris Gatling had 30 points and seven rebounds as the Dallas Mavericks defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 100-95 for a season-high three-game winning streak.
Gatling scored 14 of his points in the third quarter, when he hit all four of his field-goal attempts and all six attempts from the foul line.
Malik Sealy and Loy Vaught each scored 14 points for the Clippers.
In Milwaukee, Joe Dumars scored seven of his 29 points in a key fourth-quarter run as the Detroit Pistons won their fifth straight game, 93-85 over the Milwaukee Bucks.
Dumars, who shot 11-of-16 from the field, made a pair of free throws to cap a 10-2 spurt and give the Pistons a 79-72 lead with 7:27 left. Grant Hill added 26 points.
In New York, Allan Houston keyed a big third-quarter run with five points and Buck Williams added a season-high 15 rebounds as the New York Knicks beat the Washington Bullets 85-73.

Houston hit a three-pointer and a basket and Patrick Ewing sank a pair of jumpers during the 15-4 burst that saw New York turn a three-point lead into a 64-50 advantage with 1:40 left in the quarter. Ewing, Houston and John Starks each finished with 15 points apiece for the Knicks.

In Phoenix, Wesley Person scored 11 of his career-high 29 points in the decisive third quarter to lead the revitalised Phoenix Suns to a 93-76 victory over the reeling San Antonio Spurs, spoiling the coaching debut of Gregg Popovich and the return of David Robinson.
"Our defence was ready, it was the difference in the game tonight," Suns coach Danny Ainge said.
The Spurs, who fell to 3-16, fired coach Bob Hill earlier in the day and replaced him with general manager Popovich.

In Portland, Gerald Wilkins scored 14 of his 18 points in the fourth quarter as the Orlando Magic, bolstered by the return of Penny Hardaway and Dennis Scott, snapped a four-game losing streak with a 99-93 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.
Scott scored 18 points, Rony Seikaly added 17 and Hardaway 16 for Orlando.
Clifford Robinson scored 33 points and Rasheed Wallace added 20 points and 10 rebounds for the Blazers.
In Toronto, Joe Smith had a career-high 36 points and 17 rebounds as the Golden State Warriors began a three-game road trip with a 101-91 victory over the Toronto Raptors.
Smith keyed a decisive second-quarter run, then added 10 points in the fourth quarter as Golden State won for the fourth time in six games.

At Utah, Karl Malone scored 10 of his 22 points in a pivotal third-quarter run and Greg Ostertag added 21 points and 15 rebounds as the Utah Jazz won their 15th straight game, with a 110-86 victory over the Indiana Pacers.
John Stockton added 11 points and nine assists for the Jazz.

In Los Angeles, Shaquille O'Neal had 27 points and 13 rebounds and Eddie Jones made two free throws with 9.1 seconds left to lift the Los Angeles Lakers to their third straight win, 92-90 over the Sacramento Kings.
After Mitch Richmond's three-pointer tied the game, 90-90, with 1:52 remaining, Jones sank two free throws with 9.1 seconds to go to break the deadlock.
